description:
SIEM-ready audit export (beta) is an Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation project to let Redwood Inference customers reliably export audit events to their security monitoring stack (initial sinks: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, and S3). The project’s goals are: (1) provide a customer-configurable export pipeline with strong delivery guarantees (at-least-once with dedupe guidance, durable buffering, retry/backoff, and explicit failure states), (2) support filtering to reduce noise/cost (by event type, actor, workspace/tenant, environment, time window, and optionally IP/region), (3) publish a stable, versioned audit event schema suitable for SIEM correlation, and (4) make the feature operable (dashboards, SLOs, runbooks, replay tools) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope includes: an "audit-export" control-plane service (configuration + credentials + state), a delivery worker subsystem (queue/checkpointing/retries/DLQ), sink connectors (Splunk HEC, Datadog, S3), filtering rules and validation, customer-facing Console UX (create/export destinations, test delivery, view health), and documentation for setup + security posture. Out of scope for beta: dozens of SIEM vendors, full historical backfill for all tenants, and customer-specific field mappings beyond the published schema.

Key stakeholders: Security Engineering (Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei) owns audit schema/export security; Product Security & Compliance PM (Naomi Feldman) owns requirements/beta definition; Platform Control Plane (Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Benji Okafor) owns config APIs and reliability primitives; SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant) owns SLOs/alerts/runbooks; Console (Chloe Martin, Felix Schneider, Svetlana Petrenko) owns UX; Solutions Engineering (Colin O’Donnell, Fatima Noor) supports beta customers; GRC (Olga Petrov) ensures compliance/evidence alignment.

Phases and timeline (typical 10–12 weeks to beta):
- Discovery + requirements: confirm event taxonomy, customer SIEM needs, and compliance constraints; select beta customers.
- Architecture + ADRs: choose delivery semantics, partitioning/checkpoint strategy, connector auth models, and schema versioning.
- Build MVP: export destinations + queue/worker + initial sinks; basic filters; minimal Console UI; docs.
- Beta hardening: scale testing, backpressure controls, failure visibility, replay tooling, and on-call runbooks.
- Launch + iteration: controlled enablement (feature flag), success metrics (delivery latency, drop rate, connector errors), and feedback loop into GA planning.

Primary deliverables: PRD + design spec, ADRs, audit schema definition and mapping docs, operational SLOs/runbooks, beta release notes, customer setup guides, and a set of implementation artifacts (Linear tickets, GitHub PRs, Slack coordination threads, support tickets, customer calls/emails/CRM records).

files.description: PRD for the beta: target customers, problems solved, scope/non-goals, required sinks (Splunk/Datadog/S3), filtering requirements, delivery guarantees, pricing/packaging assumptions, success metrics, and rollout plan (feature flag + beta contract language).

End-to-end design spec: event flow, config model, filtering DSL, checkpointing strategy, retry/DLQ behavior, idempotency/deduplication guidance, and connector-level semantics (HEC acknowledgements, Datadog intake responses, S3 object naming/partitioning).

Published internal schema reference for Audit Event v1: fields, types, required/optional properties, versioning approach, PII rules/redaction guidance, and examples for common events (login, key rotation, RBAC change, export config change).
Feature overview page for internal teams: what the export does, supported destinations, limitations for beta, how filtering works, and links to runbooks/FAQ/setup guides.
ADR deciding delivery semantics (at-least-once), dedupe keys, ordering expectations, and how replay/backfill is handled; includes trade-offs vs exactly-once and impact on sink implementations.
ADR for Splunk HEC connector: auth options, HEC ACK usage, batching strategy, backoff rules, event size limits, and error classification (auth vs throttling vs schema).
ADR for S3 sink: object naming conventions, partition keys (tenant/date/hour), compression format, SSE-KMS support, and how to avoid duplicate objects under at-least-once delivery.
System doc for the new audit-export control-plane service: APIs, data model, state machine (enabled/paused/degraded), dependency graph (queue, secrets store), and ownership/oncall routing.
SLO definition for audit export: end-to-end delivery latency, success rate, backlog bounds, and alerting thresholds; includes separate SLOs for Hosted vs Private deployments.
Runbook: diagnosing export lag, draining backlog safely, replaying a time window, handling poison-pill events, connector credential rotation issues, and escalation paths.

Security risk assessment for beta: threat model, data exposure risks (misconfigured destinations), credential handling, tenant isolation concerns, and mitigation plan (rate limits, validations, audit trails of export config changes).
Customer-facing security FAQ draft for AEs/SEs: what events are included, retention, encryption, delivery guarantees, filtering options, how duplicates are handled, and typical SIEM onboarding steps.
Step-by-step setup guide for Splunk HEC: configuring token/index, validating TLS, test event delivery, troubleshooting common errors, and recommended dashboards/queries.
Setup guide for Datadog: choosing intake endpoint, API key scoping, log parsing suggestions, tag mapping, and troubleshooting rate limits/429s.
Beta release notes: enabled-by-flag, supported sinks, known limitations, migration notes for schema changes, and operational caveats (duplicates possible, recommended dedupe logic).
Working doc: beta customer selection criteria, onboarding checklist, weekly feedback questions, success metrics, and comms templates for CS/SE.
Early API sketch for export destination CRUD, filter rule validation, and health endpoints; includes open questions and alternative shapes before Confluence spec was finalized.
Draft plan for metrics/logs/traces: per-sink success/failure counters, backlog depth, delivery latency histograms, DLQ volume, and suggested dashboards.
Spreadsheet-style table: connector test cases (auth failure, throttling, partial batch failures), filter correctness tests, high-volume soak tests, and chaos/retry scenarios.
Notes for Private deployments: required Kubernetes resources, network egress needs, secrets integration, and upgrade considerations for the exporter components.
Internal GTM notes: how to talk about SIEM-ready export, common customer objections, competitor comparisons, and suggested proof points for security reviews.
Initiative ticket: define beta scope and success criteria for SIEM-ready audit export; includes target launch window, beta gating, and stakeholder sign-offs.
Define audit event taxonomy and required fields for SIEM correlation (actor, target, request id, tenant, IP/geo); aligns Security Eng + GRC.
Beta customer shortlist + onboarding plan (CS/SE coordination), including which sinks each customer needs and constraints (VPC/on-prem, data residency).
Packaging decision: whether SIEM export is included in enterprise compliance bundle vs add-on; includes pricing guidance and contract language considerations.
Define customer-facing docs requirements for beta (setup guides, dedupe guidance, limitations) and owners for each deliverable.
Project epic: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) engineering tracker; contains milestones, sub-issues, dependency graph, and rollout checklist.
Implement audit-export destination model (type=splunk|datadog|s3), credential storage, and enable/disable state machine in control plane.
Build filtering engine for audit events (include/exclude by event_type, actor, resource, environment); includes validation and safe defaults.
Queue + worker design: durable buffering, checkpointing per destination, retries with exponential backoff, and DLQ with operator tooling.
Splunk HEC connector implementation (batching, optional HEC ACK, error handling taxonomy, metrics).
Datadog Logs intake connector implementation (endpoint selection by region, request signing/API key use, throttling behavior).
S3 sink implementation: partitioning, compression, SSE-KMS, and idempotent object naming strategy.
Audit schema v1 publication + schema evolution plan (version field, backward compatibility rules, examples).
Add exporter health endpoints and per-destination status in API (last_success_at, last_error, backlog_estimate).
Console backend endpoints for managing export destinations and testing delivery (send test event, verify credentials).
Console UI: SIEM export configuration page (create destination, filters, health widget, error messages) behind a feature flag.
Observability: dashboards + alerts for export success rate, latency, DLQ growth, and connector error spikes.
Rate limiting / backpressure controls to prevent export pipeline from impacting primary API latency; includes load-shedding plan.
Security hardening: credential encryption, RBAC permissions for managing exports, and audit logging of export config changes.
Replay tooling: operator command/API to replay a time window to a destination; includes safeguards against accidental replays.
Private deployment packaging: helm chart updates and installer wiring for exporter components; document required network egress.
Design ticket: Console IA for “Security → Audit Export” including destination list, create flow, and destination detail/health states.
Design ticket: error/validation UX for filters and credentials (inline field errors, retry guidance, copyable error IDs).
Design ticket: health visualization + troubleshooting panel (last delivered, backlog estimate, common errors, links to docs).
PR: Add destination config schema + validation for Splunk/Datadog/S3, including sample configs and unit tests.
PR: Implement durable queue consumer with retries/backoff and DLQ write path; includes metrics stubs for backlog depth.
PR: Splunk HEC connector with optional ACK support; includes batching limits and structured error classification.
PR: Datadog logs connector (regional endpoints, throttle handling, request retries) plus integration tests with mock server.
PR: S3 sink writer with hourly partitions, gzip compression, SSE-KMS config, and idempotent object naming.

PR: Customer documentation draft for SIEM-ready audit export beta, including Splunk and Datadog setup and dedupe guidance.

HubSpot company record: healthcare SaaS with Datadog-centric observability; notes on HIPAA-adjacent constraints, need for audit export filtering, and POC next steps.
